definition: Phlegmatic means calm and unemotional; not easily excited or upset.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word phlegmatic. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know phlegmatic should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: Marta, the building's phlegmatic superintendent, greeted the burst pipe on the fourth floor the way she greeted everything — 'Right,' she said, and went for the wrench.
Calm can describe anyone's quiet hour — milder than phlegmatic, which is calm installed at the factory, running in every weather.
Stony goes further than phlegmatic: past unexcitable into unreadable, with even the warmth switched off.

Unflappable means impossible to rattle, whatever arrives — it reports the result. Phlegmatic names the temperament underneath: a person built so level that the surge never comes in the first place. Someone can train themselves unflappable for a job; the phlegmatic were simply issued that way.

Composed means your feelings are held in check right now — control that takes effort, the slow breath before the speech. Phlegmatic is composed as a permanent setting, no breath needed, because nothing is surging underneath. Anyone can be composed for an hour; the phlegmatic are level for life.

The harbor ferry has had louder captains, but none steadier than Captain Mbeki.
Crew members trade stories the way sailors do — the waterspout of '09, the winter the engine quit mid-channel — and every story ends the same way, with Mbeki unhurried at the wheel.
